Before joining Theory, Kelly helped scale Uniqlo’s US expansion. He succeeds Dinesh Tandon, who will transition into the co-chief operating officer role, as well as returning to his role as CEO of Theory China.

It has been revealed that organization comments: “James has been an instrumental leader for Theory over the past several years, bringing strategic vision, operational excellence and a deep understanding of our business,” said Kazumi Yanai, chairman of Theory. “As James assumes the role of global CEO and Dinesh focuses his leadership on one of our most vital markets, we are further expanding our global organization and positioning Theory for continued success around the world.”.

Background: Charlotte Fournet, the niece of Kering chair François-Henri Pinault, has been named CEO of jewelry maison Pomellato, succeeding Kering Italia president Sabina Belli. Fournet joined Saint Laurent in 2014 before moving to Gucci in 2019 and then Bottega Veneta in 2020, where she climbed the merchandising ladder to become director just over three years ago. Krizia Cucurachi, who joined Dodo in 2024 as global product and brand director, has been promoted to CEO. Prior to joining the brand, she spent more than a decade at Swarovski across several senior leadership positions. Both will report to Kering Jewelry CEO Jean-Marc Duplaix, based in Milan.

According to recent reports, organization comments: “Jewelry is a strategic growth pillar for Kering. Pomellato and Dodo are two highly distinctive houses with strong identities and tremendous potential. Charlotte’s extensive experience across several Kering houses and Krizia’s strong track record in brand-building and transformation make them ideally positioned to lead the next phase of growth for Pomellato and Dodo,” Duplaix remarked in a statement.

Background: Sabina Belli, who joined Kering as CEO of Pomellato in 2015, has been named president of Kering Italia. Before joining the French luxury group, Belli held senior marketing and executive roles at WPP, L’Oréal Luxe and LVMH, spanning the likes of Christian Dior Parfums, Moët Hennessy, Veuve Clicquot, and Bvlgari. Since this April, she has also led Kering Accademia per le Eccellenze, a Kering initiative dedicated to preserving and promoting Italian craftsmanship, alongside serving on the directors board of the Kering Foundation. In her new role, Belli will report directly to CEO Luca de Meo, based in Milan.

Recent findings suggest that company comments: “Italy occupies a unique place in Kering’s history, identity, and future. Its creativity, craftsmanship, and industrial excellence are at the heart of our houses and the long-term vitality of the luxury industry,” de Meo remarked in a statement. “Sabina brings a deep understanding of the Italian luxury ecosystem and a strong ability to build partnerships across business, education and public institutions.”.

Background: Kristin Bauer, who spent three years as chief supply chain officer for sneaker retailer Foot Locker, will join Converse as chief operating officer. As parent company Nike works to revive its Converse business, following consecutive quarters of slow sales, it is rebuilding a leadership structure to help propel growth. Bauer will report to Nike COO Venky Alagirisamy.

Manufacturer comments: “We are excited to welcome Kristin and look forward to the perspective she will bring as we continue to build momentum for the brand,” Nike stated in a statement.

Background: Jane Ewing has been named chief commercial officer and executive vice president of Nike, reporting directly to CEO Elliott Hill. She joins after a 14-year tenure at Walmart, most recently serving as interim CEO for Sam’s Club China. She also previously held senior leadership roles at Diageo. In her new role, Ewing will lead Nike’s global marketplace organization, including Sales and Nike Direct.

Company’s comments: “Jane’s experience, leadership and global perspective will help us continue this work and accelerate growth across Nike Direct and wholesale. Her role is vital to creating even stronger connections between brand, product and marketplace while serving athletes* and consumers around the world,” Hill said in a statement.

Industry observers note that background: The British Fashion Council (BFC) has confirmed that David Pemsel is stepping down as chair after four years in the position and 10 years on the executive board. During his time as chair, the BFC achieved record revenue figures (£14 million in FY2024/25), raised £7.2 million through the BFC Foundation and secured a multi-million-pound investment from the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport. Pemsel also appointed Laura Weir as BFC CEO in early 2025. A successor will be announced in September.

Sources indicate that company comments: “David has been an exceptional chair and an unwavering champion of British fashion. His leadership has helped strengthen the British Fashion Council as an organization, creating the stability, governance and long-term foundations that enable us to deliver our ambitions for the industry,” Weir noted in a statement.

Background: Alexandre Oulès has been named chief operating officer for the LVMH beauty division, reporting to Véronique Courtois, president and CEO of Parfums Christian Dior and of the LVMH Group’s beauty division. According to the internal announcement, his latest role will “oversee manufacturing, supply chain, and purchasing across the beauty division, driving stronger convergence between maisons across all three functions”. Oulès joins from Balenciaga, where he was appointed COO in October 2023. He previously held roles at L’Oréal, Guerlain, Celine and Moët Hennessy.

Company’s comment: “I am delighted to welcome back Alexandre, whose pursuit of operational excellence is widely recognized. His knowledge of the group and the specificities of the beauty world will strongly contribute to the overall efficiency of our operations,” Courtois said.

In a recent development, background: Maya Dukes, who previously worked at Macy’s as head of graphic design (2001-2007), will return to the retailer as executive creative director. Dukes has more than two decades of experience leading creative strategy for some of the world’s best-known consumer brands, including her most recent role leasing global creative at Delta Airlines. At Macy’s, Dukes will report to CMO Sharon Otterman, overseeing the organization’s creative and storytelling to bring the Macy’s brand back to life and help propel its Bold New Chapter strategy.

Industry observers note that company comments: “I am excited to welcome Maya back to Macy’s. Her experience translating brand strategy into compelling storytelling, elevating the customer experience and modernizing the creative process will be critical as we strengthen Macy’s for the future,” Otterman remarked in a statement.

Sources indicate that background: Skims has appointed its first-ever chief design officer, Erin Magee, best known for her time at Supreme, where she spent over 20 years. Most recently she held the role of chief creative officer, under which she led the brand’s creative vision, design, product development, and product strategy across apparel, accessories, collaborations, and special projects. Skims has also promoted Kim Schraub, who has been on board since Skims’s founding, to chief brand officer from her previous role as creative director. In her new role, Schraub will balance creative and commercial. Prior to joining Skims, Schraub worked at Abercrombie, Victoria’s Secret Pink and Yeezy.

Firm comments: “Erin brings an unparalleled creative vision and a proven ability to build brands that transcend fashion and become cultural touchstones,” CEO and co-founder Jens Grede stated in a statement. “Her eye for design, her deep understanding of product and her instinct for what resonates make her exactly the right person to lead Skims into its next era. We’re incredibly excited to welcome her to the team.”.

According to recent reports, “Kim has been with us since before Skims existed. She helped turn an idea into a brand that people genuinely love,” Kim Kardashian, Skims chief creative officer and co-founder, noted in a statement. “Her creative instincts have helped shape everything about how Skims shows up in the world, and this promotion is a reflection of the enormous impact she has had, and the trust Jens and I have in her vision. I can’t wait to see where she takes us next.”.

Background: Vuori has appointed Carey Collins Krug as CMO. She joins from Abercrombie & Fitch, where she spent the last seven years, four of which she held the CMO role. Prior to Abercrombie, Collins Krug held top marketing positions at David Yurman, Ralph Lauren and Donna Karan. At Vuori, she will lead the brand’s cross-channel marketing initiatives, and focus on global expansion.

Company comments: “Carey brings the kind of brand-building, consumer engagement and cross-functional marketing leadership that will be instrumental as Vuori enters its next chapter of growth,” Joe Kudla, founder and CEO of Vuori, mentioned in a statement. “Her experience helping global lifestyle brands sharpen their storytelling and build deeper connections with consumers aligns closely with where we’re headed as we continue to scale.”.

Background: Rains has appointed Tom Bettinson as CEO, succeeding co-founder Daniel Brix Hesselager, who will transition into a business development role after leading the company for a year and a half. Since the initiatives core to Brix Hesselager’s transformation initiative, in particular retail development, have been implemented, the focus will now shift to driving commercial success through these investments. Bettinson first joined Rains in 2017, helping to establish the brand’s UK business, before stepping away and rejoining as CSO, with responsibility for all company sales channels, in 2025.

Company comments: “I stepped into the CEO role to lead a fundamental transformation of our concept and organization. It was an extensive undertaking that required swift decision-making. Today, the foundation is in place, and the time is right to pass the baton,” Brix Hesselager mentioned in a statement. “The priority now is ensuring excellence in execution and driving commercial success across all areas of the business. Tom is the right person to lead that next phase.”.

Industry observers note that background: Pandora has appointed André Branch as president of North America, one of the Danish jewelry brand’s largest growth markets. Branch brings more than 25 years of experience across global consumer, beauty and lifestyle brands, most recently having served as CEO at Ariana Grande’s R.e.m. Beauty. At Pandora, he will lead the business’s next phase of regional growth, focusing specifically on enhancing customer relevance and brand appeal. Branch is succeeding Luciano Rodembusch, who departed the firm in February.

According to recent reports, firm comments: “André is a highly accomplished commercial leader with a strong track record of driving growth across global consumer businesses. His ability to combine strategic clarity with disciplined execution makes him exactly the right person to lead our North America business and drive the next phase of growth in the region,” chief commercial officer Massimo Basei remarked in a statement.

According to recent reports, background: Skims has hired Jasmine Sevan as vice president of communications. With nearly two decades of experience, Sevan will play a key role in advancing Skims’s global communication efforts, further strengthening its position at the intersection of fashion, culture, and innovation. She most recently served as global communications and brand partnerships director at Victoria Beckham, where she led the comms strategy during a period of significant growth, spurred by the brand’s Paris Fashion Week debut, collaborations with Mango and Gap, and the global launch of Netflix documentary, Victoria Beckham. At Skims, Sevan will report to chief communications officer Tracy Nguyen.

Company comments: “Jasmine is an exceptional communications leader with a sharp strategic mindset and a deep understanding of how brands shape culture,” Nguyen noted in a statement. “Her experience building reputation for fashion’s most-respected brands, alongside her relationships across media, fashion and entertainment, makes her an incredible addition to Skims.”.

Background: Birgit Kretschmer will succeed Harm Ohlmeyer as chief financial officer of Adidas. Kretschmer spent 25 years of her career at the sportswear giant, following a six-year tenure as CFO of German fast fashion firm C&A. Harm, who helped with the appointment of Kretschmer as his successor, will stay close to Adidas, ensuring a smooth leadership transition.

Company comments: “I am extremely happy that we have signed Birgit to be the successor of Harm. She knows the industry, she knows Adidas, and she has added the knowledge of cost discipline working as the CFO of a vertical retailer like C&A. I really look forward to welcoming her back on our team,” CEO Bjørn Gulden said in the company’s half-year earnings release.

Background: John Schlifske has exited the Kohl’s board after nearly 15 years of service, stepping down as chair to enter retirement. In his place, Wendy Arlin, who has been a director since 2023, will take on the chair role. Arlin has more than three decades of finance and consumer brand experience.

Manufacturer comments: “With deep financial and retail expertise, Wendy provides valuable perspective to both the board and the management team. She has been a valued voice and a natural leader in the boardroom since joining, and I look forward to working with her in this fresh capacity,” said Michael J. Bender, Kohl’s CEO and board director, in a statement.

According to recent reports, background: Whoop, the wearable fitness tech brand, has named Kyle Leahy as chief commercial officer. She will oversee the company’s commercial operations as it continues to scale across international markets and fresh channels, specifically its healthcare go-to-market strategy. Leahy comes from Glossier, where she transformed the beauty brand from a direct-to-consumer business into a global omnichannel company, bringing it to profitability during her three-year tenure as CEO.

Recent findings suggest that manufacturer comments: “Kyle has a proven track record of leading strong brands through rapid growth. She knows how to expand premium distribution and build the right partnerships without losing what makes a brand special. That experience will be critical as we bring Whoop to more people around the world,” founder and CEO Will Ahmed stated in a statement.

Sources indicate that background: Skims has promoted Tracy Nguyen, formerly executive VP of communications and entertainment, as chief communications officer. Nguyen, who has been at Skims since 2024, will continue to lead global communications for the intimates brand, as well as collaborations and cultural activations across entertainment, sports, and brand partnerships. Most notably, the executive was key in building the partnership between Skims and Nike last year, and was subsequently appointed co-general manager of the venture — a role she will continue in alongside.

Tech giant comments: “From her time as a trusted advisor across my entire brand portfolio — when Skims was just an idea — to joining Skims in a formal executive capacity more than two years ago, Tracy has been an incredible partner and leader. She understands the brand at its core — how to protect it, grow it, and put it in front of the right audiences at the right moments,” said Kim Kardashian, Skims chief creative officer and co-founder, in a statement.

Recent findings suggest that background: Manolo Blahnik has appointed former Chloé executive Kimberly Mimnaugh as managing director of Americas. Beyond her most recent role as VP of North America retail at Chloé, Mimnaugh’s luxury commercial experience spans various leadership positions at the likes of Brunello Cucinelli, and Theory and Helmut Lang. At Manolo Blahnik, she will deliver the commercial strategy for the brand’s Newly introduced York-based subsidiary, across retail, wholesale and e-commerce.

Tech giant comments: “Kimberly brings an exceptional combination of luxury retail expertise and commercial leadership. Her proven ability to accelerate direct-to-consumer growth while maintaining a strong wholesale business makes her ideally placed to lead this next phase of our growth in the Americas. I look forward to working closely with her,” CEO Kristina Blahnik mentioned in a statement.

Background: John Smedley, the British knitwear brand that’s been in operation for more than 240 years, has revamped its executive line-up. Jess McGuire-Dudley, managing director since April 2025, has been named CEO, while Bryan Jackson is returning to the manufacturer as senior independent director, after retiring last year following 11 years as chair. Latest recruits include COO Brian Lancaster and CFO Stuart Pannell.

Firm comments: “Today, we announce the appointment of a strengthened executive leadership team that combines deep industry expertise, operational excellence, and a shared commitment to securing the long-term future of John Smedley. With ambitious aims to strengthen John Smedley’s position as one of Britain’s most-respected luxury manufacturing brands, this C-suite will take the company into its next phase of growth,” McGuire-Dudley remarked in a statement shared with Vogue Business.

Recent findings suggest that background: Yann Musquin has been appointed managing director of LVMH fragrance brands, reporting to Véronique Courtois, president and CEO of Parfums Christian Dior and the LVMH beauty division. Musquin’s appointment comes after Romain Spitzer, who led LVMH fragrance brands for 10 years, was named CEO of Kering-owned house Bottega Veneta.

Industry observers note that musquin joined Parfums Christian Dior in 2008, where he was eventually appointed international fragrance marketing director in 2013, overseeing the creation of the Sauvage fragrance, as well as the development of Miss Dior and the Collection Privée Christian Dior. From 2021, he was fragrance and beauty director at Louis Vuitton, before becoming chief brand officer for Givenchy Parfums and Beauty in December 2024.

In this new role, Musquin will lead the strategic vision for LVMH fragrance brands, with the mission to strengthen the desirability of Givenchy Parfums and Kenzo Parfums, as well as develop the portfolio with new fragrance and beauty expressions.

In a recent development, organization comments: “I had the opportunity to work extensively with Yann on fragrance development at the Parfums Christian Dior. I am convinced that his remarkable expertise in fragrances and the beauty world, his sense of excellence, and his creative vision will make it possible to strengthen the desirability of our Givenchy Parfums and Kenzo Parfums. Yann has all the qualities to pursue the development of our portfolio with ambition and success,” Courtois stated in a statement.

Recent findings suggest that background: Hélène de Tissot has been named global chief financial officer of Chanel, following the retirement of Philippe Blondiaux earlier this month. With more than 30 years of global leadership experience, Tissot will continue to enhance Chanel’s finance function, specifically doubling down on long-term investments in creation, craftsmanship, and the client experience.

Prior to this, Tissot served as group executive VP of finance and technology at wine and spirits group Pernod Ricard for eight years. At Chanel, the executive will report directly to global CEO Leena Nair in London, starting October 2026, before assuming full responsibilities from January 2027.

Background: Kate Spade has appointed Jonathan Saunders executive creative director, the Tapestry-owned brand announced on Tuesday. Saunders joins from H&M-owned brand & Other Stories, where he was chief creative officer for one year. Saunders announced his departure from the brand earlier this month. In addition to running his own label for 12 years, until 2015, Scotland-born Saunders has worked at brands including Diane von Furstenberg, Calvin Klein, Tiffany & Co., Pucci and Alexander McQueen. He’ll relocate to New York for the Kate Spade role.

Sources indicate that company comments: “Kate Spade has always stood for positivity, femininity and a touch of wit,” Eva Erdmann, CEO of Kate Spade New York, said in a statement. “Jonathan shares our consumer obsession, and he understands the heart of our brand. He’s also a collaborative leader and I’m excited to work together to introduce an uplifting vision of luxury to a new generation of consumers.”.

Background: Bruno Pavlovsky, president of Chanel fashion and Chanel SAS, has been president of French governing body Fédération de la Haute Couture et de la Mode (FHCM), which notably oversees Paris Fashion Week, since July 2022. At FHCM’s annual general meeting on Friday, Pavlovsky was re-elected for another four-year mandate. Meanwhile, FHCM executive president Pascal Morand, who has been in the role since 2016, has also been confirmed, alongside a latest board of directors and executive committee.

The new executive committee, which comprises Chanel’s Pavlovsky, Saint Laurent’s Cédric Charbit, Rick Owens’s Elsa Lanzo, Hermès’s Guillaume de Seynes, LVMH’s Sidney Toledano and FHCM’s Morand, welcomes a new member: Alaïa’s Myriam Serrano, who will succeed Anouck Duranteau-Loeper, the former Isabel Marant CEO who recently joined Saint Laurent. Jacquemus’s Sarah Benady and Alaïa’s Serrano will join the board of directors.

The board of directors also approved four new members: Alaïa, The Row, Tom Ford, and Zimmermann.

Background: Chanel has revealed that global CFO Philippe Blondiaux is retiring after 15 years in the role. Blondiaux joined Chanel in 2011 after an international career spanning finance and business leadership at Nestlé and PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC). A future global CFO will be announced in due course.

According to recent reports, company comments: “Throughout Philippe’s tenure, his ability to combine strategic vision with operational excellence has allowed Chanel to invest confidently in the future while maintaining strong financial performance,” Chanel stated in a statement. “He has been instrumental in strengthening our financial position and long-term ambitions, driving modernization efforts, major investments in real estate, and expanding our global boutique network.”.

Industry observers note that “Beyond his responsibilities as global CFO and member of the board of Chanel, Philippe has been a widely trusted advisor and valued partner across the house. He has also served as a board member of Fondation Chanel since 2024, actively contributing to Chanel’s philanthropic and social impact initiatives,” the statement added.

According to recent reports, background: Alessio Vannetti has been appointed CEO of La Perla Atelier, joining La Perla Atelier a few months after the completion of its acquisition in September 2025 through Luxury Holdings LLC, the investment firm of American billionaire and former Expedia CEO Peter Kern. Vannetti previously held senior roles at Prada and Zegna, before joining Gucci’s leadership team under Marco Bizzarri and Alessandro Michele.

From 2020 to July 2023, he served at Valentino as EVP, chief brand officer and member of the executive committee before returning to Gucci in 2023 as EVP, chief brand officer, a role he held until the end of 2024. Over the past 18 months, he has served as strategic advisor to Etnia Eyewear Culture, a Barcelona-based eyewear organization, and to Allemandi / Intesa Sanpaolo, where he contributed to redefining the editorial and commercial model of art publication Il Giornale dell’Arte.

Paolo Vannucchi, who has served as CEO since the reopening of the Bologna Atelier last December, will take on a strategic advisory role to ensure an orderly transition through the end of the current financial year.

Company’s comment: “We first met Alessio earlier this year, and from those early conversations it became clear that his understanding of what La Perla is — and what it is capable of becoming — was both precise and expansive,” Kirsten and Peter Kern, principal shareholders of La Perla Atelier, said in a statement. “With Alessio leading the business, together with the exceptional teams in Bologna and across the company, we are confident in the future of La Perla and in the next chapter we are building together.”.

It has been revealed that background: Alexis Rollier will lead PVH’s global finance organization and oversee all aspects of the organization’s global financial moves, reporting to CEO Stefan Larsson. Rollier joins PVH from Sephora, which sits under LVMH, where he has served as global chief operating officer and global CFO since 2018. He spent 14 years at the beauty retailer, before which he held senior roles at Guerlain, Kingfisher and LVMH.

Organization comments: “Alexis is a unique global finance leader, who brings highly relevant expertise across multi-brand and omni-channel retail, deep financial and operational experience, and a strong track record of driving disciplined growth with profit expansion,” PVH CEO Stefan Larsson said in a statement. “As we continue our journey to build Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger into their full potential, Alexis’s experience connecting consumer-facing strategies with effective financial steering will help drive long-term shareholder value.”.

Background: Brooke Bobb has been appointed vice president, fashion director, of Nordstrom. Bobb — who will report to chief merchandising officer Jamie Nordstrom — will lead Nordstrom’s fashion direction and editorial vision and will work alongside merchant leaders and attend global fashion weeks on behalf of the organization. Previously, Bobb served as fashion news director at Harper’s Bazaar, leading fashion news and trends coverage across digital platforms. Prior to that, she held roles at Amazon Luxury Stores, T: The New York Times Style Magazine, and Vogue.

It has been revealed that tech giant comments: “Brooke has a strong combination of editorial credibility and commercial instinct. She understands how people discover and engage with style today, and how to translate that into something meaningful for our business. We believe her vision will elevate how we show up for our customers, our brand partners, and our teams,” Jamie Nordstrom stated in a statement.

Background: Valérie Duport has been elected president of the board of Villa Noailles, the association that organizes the International Festival of Fashion, Photography and Accessories of Hyères, succeeding Pascale Mussard, whose term is coming to an end after a decade as president. Duport began her career at Chanel in the late 1980s, where she held roles in press relations and communications within the fragrance and beauty division, before moving to watches and fine jewelry. Over the years, she rose to become international director of press services and external relations for the house. Later, Duport joined Kering as director of communications and brand image. Today, she serves as a strategic advisor to leading institutions and companies.

In a recent development, duport said: “We are writing a latest chapter in a remarkable story. This house has celebrated its 100th anniversary, the fashion festival its 40th, and Design Parade its 20th. These milestones reflect the strength and enduring nature of a unique cultural project, driven by teams whose commitment and energy I would like to acknowledge. More than ever, our times call for freedom, creativity, and boldness. It is our responsibility to nurture, support, and bring to light the talents of the next generation of creators.”.

The next edition of the Hyères fashion festival will be held from October 15 to 18, 2026.

Company comments: “This appointment is part of the upcoming momentum initiated following the appointment of Hugo Lucchino as managing director of Villa Noailles last October. Valérie Duport’s appointment came about naturally, following a spontaneous discussion with Pascale Mussard and in consultation with the public partners, reflecting a shared commitment to ensuring a smooth and consistent transition,” Villa Noailles stated in a statement.

Valérie Duport and Hugo Lucchino, respectively.

According to recent reports, background: J.Crew has appointed Kathleen Van Nest Pierce as brand president, a newly created role for the American lifestyle label. Pierce joins from Dyson, where she served as global beauty president for four years, helping triple its technology portfolio and cement its position as a definitive leader in the premium beauty device market. At J.Crew, she will lead the brand’s merchandising, design, marketing, and retail teams to accelerate business momentum and deliver long-term growth. Pierce will report to Libby Wadle, CEO of parent tech giant J.Crew Group.

Recent findings suggest that organization comments: “J.Crew’s status as an iconic American brand holds great meaning to its customers globally, and we look forward to Kathleen’s contributions,” said J.Crew Group chair Kevin Ulrich in a statement. “Moreover, Kathleen’s expertise in scaling global consumer brands makes her the ideal leader to build on J.Crew’s foundation and accelerate its growth. I am excited to have an executive of her caliber leading the brand into its next chapter.”.

In a recent development, background: Alice Temperley is exiting Temperley London, the womenswear label she founded in 2000. Temperley has stood as creative director of her brand since the beginning, shaping the house through an aesthetic incorporating craft, embellishment, and bohemian elegance. In 2023, the British designer sold a controlling stake in her label to Dubai-based retail firm Times Square Group, before staying on as creative director amid a flagship store opening and wholesale relaunch. Looking ahead, she will be focusing on a new independent project, in collaboration with her creative network, family, and the muses, who have so far shaped her vision.

Tech giant comments: “I am enormously proud of everything I have built at Temperley London. It has been the creative home of my life for over two decades. The time is right for me to pursue a new direction, one that allows me to follow long-held passions, with the people I love, on things that feel completely true to who I am as a designer,” Temperley said in a statement.

Recent findings suggest that background: Klitos Teklos will join Fresh York fashion label Tory Burch in a newly created chief brand officer role, leading the company’s global brand strategy. Teklos will partner with the brand’s longstanding creative director Honor Brodie, overseeing global marketing, social media, and visual merchandising, reporting directly to chief creative officer Tory Burch and CEO Pierre-Yves Roussel.

Recent findings suggest that teklos joins from the namesake brand architecture agency he founded in 2023, which has served clients spanning The Row, Sol de Janeiro and most recently Gap Inc., where he led the development of its beauty category. At Tory Burch, Teklos will focus on driving a cohesive vision across markets and channels to support long-term growth.

Company comments: “Klitos brings a rare combination of creative vision, commercial acumen, and operational rigor. He understands how to build meaningful connections with customers, and I am delighted to welcome him to our team,” Burch remarked in a statement.

Background: Balenciaga has appointed Drieke Leenknegt as chief marketing officer, reporting directly to the CEO Gianfranco Gianangeli and joining the brand’s executive committee. She brings over 25 years of leadership experience in product innovation, brand-building, and business transformation across global sports and lifestyle companies. Leenknegt spent 20 years at Nike, before serving as CMO at Timberland and then Vans, where she most recently led brand repositioning and organizational transformation.

Recent findings suggest that background: David M. Denton will join Nike as chief financial officer, succeeding Matthew Friend, who will stay on to support the transition until September 4. Denton will lead Nike’s global finance organization, supporting CEO Elliott Hill and working with the senior leadership team to guide capital allocation and spur long-term value creation. He brings with him more than 30 years of finance and operating leadership experience across global public companies, most recently at Pfizer, where he served as CFO from May 2022.

Manufacturer comments: “David is a proven public-company CFO who knows how to help great consumer brands operate with discipline and invest to win,” Nike president and CEO Elliott Hill noted in a statement. “We’re focused on doing what Nike does best: serving athletes, leading with sport, and building the most innovative products in the world. His experience, judgment, and operating rigor will help us execute against these priorities with consistency and build on the progress underway.”.

Background: Eloise Hautcoeur has been named global communications director of Loewe. In her new role, Hautcoeur will oversee PR, VIP and talents and events. She started her career at Agent Provocateur and Vivienne Westwood before senior roles at Saint Laurent and Bottega Veneta. Hautcoeur’s last role was as global communications director at Versace.

Recent findings suggest that background: Laura du Rusquec has been named CEO of Kylie Jenner’s clothing label, Khy, bringing nearly 20 years of experience leading and growing fashion and luxury brands. Before Khy, du Rusquec previously served as CEO of Danish brand Ganni and spent seven years in the role of deputy CEO at Balenciaga. Du Rusquec has also held several leadership roles within the Kering group.

Background: Rémy Baume has been named chief executive officer of Printemps Group, the French retail company that owns Printemps, Citadium, Place des Tendances, and Made In Design. After occupying operational roles at major conglomerates including at LVMH and Carrefour, Baume joined childrenswear specialist Kidiliz Group as CEO in 2013, before leading Zadig & Voltaire from 2020. At Printemps Group, he succeeds Jean-Marc Bellaiche, who exited the business last September.

In a recent development, tech giant comments: “Rémy’s career path demonstrates his ability to combine strategic vision with operational excellence in a highly competitive environment. Coupled with his in-depth understanding of transformation, retail, and branding, this makes him a major asset in securing sustainable growth for Printemps,” read a statement from the board.

According to recent reports, background: Kering brand Alexander McQueen has appointed Gianfranco D’Attis as its fresh CEO. D’Attis, who will report directly to Kering CEO Luca de Meo, will “lead the next stage in the house’s development”, working to improve financial performance and guiding the brand through its streamlining of its retail network and organization. D’Attis brings more than 25 years of international experience in the luxury industry and was most recently CEO of Prada. He previously held senior roles at LVMH and Richemont in Asia, America, and Europe.

Manufacturer comments: “I am very pleased to welcome Gianfranco to Kering. He brings a powerful combination of strategic vision, operational rigor and deep luxury expertise. His ability to sharpen brand identity while driving disciplined execution will be critical as we refocus Alexander McQueen and unlock its full potential. I am confident that, together with the teams, he will lead the house into its next phase of development,” Kering CEO Luca de Meo said in a statement.

Sources indicate that background: At Kering’s 2026 Annual General Meeting (AGM), shareholders approved the appointments of Laurent Kleitman and Marie-Hélène Chenut to the manufacturer’s board of directors. Kleitman is the group CEO of Mandarin Oriental. Prior to joining Mandarin Oriental, he served as president and CEO of Parfums Christian Dior and president of Coty’s consumer beauty division. Chenut held various roles at Chanel, before leading the haute couture division, as well as its haute couture and ready-to-wear ateliers for nine years. The appointments follow the departures of Maureen Chiquet and Yonca Dervisoglu, who both reached the end of their terms.

Organization comments: “Marie-Hélène Chenut’s industry expertise, understanding of business, operational and brand-related concerns, and ability to grasp the expectations of a demanding international clientele will be valuable assets to the board of directors of Kering,” the group said in a statement prior to the AGM. “The board of directors of Kering will benefit from Laurent Kleitman’s expertise in managing global luxury brands, his extensive international experience and knowledge of various markets, as well as his strong financial and strategic background.”.

Recent findings suggest that background: Lanvin has named Barbara Werschine as chief executive officer of the French heritage house, succeeding Andy Lew, who served as CEO from July 2025 and will become executive president of Lanvin Group. Bringing her expertise and strong track record in luxury — previously CEO of cashmere house Éric Bompard, following leadership roles at Hermès, Celine, and Louis Vuitton — she will be steering Lanvin’s global strategy, including strengthening its European markets while accelerating development in the US and Asia-Pacific regions.

Werschine will work closely with Peter Copping, who joined Lanvin as artistic director in September 2024, in reviving the brand through a strategic product roadmap spanning women’s ready-to-wear, menswear, home, and lifestyle.

Company comments: “We are delighted to welcome Barbara Werschine to the helm of maison Lanvin. Her vision of the luxury market and deep understanding of our industry’s challenges will be major assets in guiding Lanvin through its next phase of growth, while honoring the unique identity of this iconic house,” Lew stated in a statement.

Background: John Galantic took over Tod’s as CEO in September 2024, just after the business delisted from the Italian stock exchange. He exited the Italian-based company at the end of April, citing personal reasons. The company is yet to name a replacement.

Background: Anish Agarwal has been appointed chief executive officer of Bella Hadid’s fragrance brand Orebella, leading its expansion into newly introduced markets and categories. Agarwal previously served as CEO of hair tool company T3 Micro, where he spearheaded the brand’s growth. He has also held positions at Sanex and Colgate parent company Colgate-Palmolive.

In a recent development, tech giant comments: “I was looking for a CEO who truly understands both sides — the discipline it takes to build a global business and the magic behind creating a world-class experience for our community. Anish embodies both so naturally, and to me, that means everything,” Hadid noted in a statement.

Industry observers note that background: Marco De Vincenzo has been appointed head of leather goods design at Givenchy, working under the artistic direction of Sarah Burton. The Italian designer previously served as head of leather goods at Fendi from 2008 until 2022, before a four-year tenure as creative director of Etro, overseeing womenswear, menswear, home, and kid’s. Alongside, De Vincenzo also ran his namesake brand from 2009 until 2020, when it ceased operations.

Organization comments: “Working closely with Sarah Burton, Marco De Vincenzo will contribute to accelerating the development of the maison’s leather goods category, bringing his unique vision and expertise to support Givenchy’s next chapter,” the company said.

Industry observers note that background: Mina Piccinini, who has been Moncler chief marketing and corporate strategy officer since 2023, has been named president of Moncler Grenoble, the brand’s performance and mountain line. In this role, she will report to group CEO Leo Rongone. Piccinini will also continue to hold her previous role of group chief corporate strategy officer, reporting to executive chair Remo Ruffini.

Firm comments: “In this new role, Mina will be responsible for the entire Grenoble business, guiding the end-to-end strategy to bring Moncler Grenoble to the next step in terms of brand positioning and business performance,” the company remarked in an internal announcement.

It has been revealed that background: Rod Manley, who joined the Moncler brand as chief international brand officer in January 2025, has been promoted to chief marketing officer, reporting to chief brand officer Gino Fisanotti. Prior to Moncler, Manley served as CMO of Burberry, following senior roles at Calvin Klein in New York and Armani in New York and Milan.

Company comments: “In this role, Rod will lead the development and implementation of our global and integrated marketing strategies, ensure coherence and enhance synergies across the brand, continuing to strengthen a unified, meaningful and impactful narrative across all regions and key markets,” the company mentioned in an internal announcement.

Industry observers note that background: Celebrity makeup artist Wendy Rowe has been appointed makeup artist and beauty editor of British department store Harvey Nichols. In the role, Rowe — who has worked with Nicole Kidman, Victoria Beckham, and Elle Fanning — will be shaping Harvey Nichols’s beauty content and strategy. She has also worked with brands including Chanel, Gucci and Prada. Wendy’s impressive career includes serving as artistic consultant for Burberry for 15 years, where she was instrumental in developing and launching Burberry Beauty and as creative director at Max Factor, where she led product innovation and brand evolution. Her work has shaped some of the industry’s most successful beauty rolls out, including Le Rouge.

It has been revealed that tech giant comments: “I am thrilled to be joining Harvey Nichols as beauty editor. Growing up, Harvey Nichols was always the department store that set the standard [with] the most cutting-edge curation of fashion and beauty, the place where you discovered what was next. That legacy of being a tastemaker is what excites me most about this moment,” noted Rowe. “In my latest role, I want to cut through the noise and help customers navigate the ever-evolving beauty landscape. This is about bringing my years of industry experience directly to customers, making luxury beauty accessible and understandable, while championing innovation across every aspect of the beauty experience at Harvey Nichols. We’re bringing that pioneering spirit back.”.

Sources indicate that background: In July, Donald Kohler will join Gap Inc. as global brand president and CEO of Banana Republic. Kohler hails from PVH, where he held the role of CEO of PVH Americas, overseeing Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger. Prior to this, he held senior leadership roles at Burberry, Ferragamo, and Diesel — before which, Kohler spent a decade at Gap Inc. in merchandising leadership roles across Gap, GapKids, and BabyGap.

Firm comments: “Donald is a product-driven leader with deep global expertise and an extraordinary track record of revitalizing brands to upcoming relevance with clarity, discipline, and storytelling that connects with customers to drive growth,” Gap Inc. CEO Richard Dickson stated in a statement.

Background: Swiss-based non-profit Aura Blockchain Consortium has appointed OTB Group’s Stefano Rosso as its newly introduced chair, succeeding Prada Group’s Lorenzo Bertelli, who remains on the board. Rosso has sat on Aura’s board since the Italian fashion group joined the consortium in 2021. The Aura Blockchain Consortium was founded in 2021 by LVMH, OTB Group, Prada Group, and Richemont to add digital traceability to luxury’s supply chain via blockchain technology. Today, the consortium counts more than 50 luxury brands in its organization and has registered over 80 million products on its blockchain. As part of Aura’s governance model, the role of chair rotates every five years, which a spokesperson said seeks to ensure “equality and collaboration”.

In a recent development, company comments: “Today, Aura represents far more than a technology platform. It embodies a vision for the future of luxury,” remarked Rosso. “Taking on this role is both an honor and a responsibility. In a context where trust is becoming increasingly central, our ambition is to help define a global standard that ensures transparency, protection, and value throughout the entire product lifecycle.”.

It has been revealed that background: The Brazilian-inspired beauty brand has named Jordan Saxemard as its next CEO, taking over from Heela Yang, who founded the company in 2015 and will be exiting the business. The brand was sold to L’Occitane Group in 2021, but Saxemard joined the brand in October 2025 as global chief marketing and digital officer, after leadership positions at Dyson and Coty. In Saxemard’s new role, he will be tasked with scaling Sol de Janeiro and overseeing its operations.

According to recent reports, tech giant comments: “Jordan Saxemard has already made a significant impact at Sol de Janeiro. This transition ensures continuity of leadership and positions him well to build on the brand’s strong momentum as it enters this next chapter,” mentioned Reinold Geiger, L’Occitane Group chair and CEO, in a statement.

Background: Paris-based fashion house Casablanca has named Didier Nguyen as its next CEO. Nguyen joins the brand with a CV spanning key roles at Amiri, Saint Laurent, Dior, Givenchy, and more. Now is a pivotal time for Casablanca, as the company continues to expand its presence globally and cement its place at the intersection of sport, travel, culture, and luxury. The appointment follows the transition of former CEO Frederick Lukoff, who has led the brand since 2023, into a senior advisory position.

Industry observers note that firm comments: “Didier shares the same passion for beauty, craft, and storytelling that sits at the heart of everything we do and are. We connect on so many different levels of culture and values, there is a genuine respect and I am excited to build the next chapter of Casablanca together,” Charaf Tajer, founder and creative director, mentioned in a statement.

Background: Heidi O’Neill, who exited her role as Nike’s president of consumer, product and brand in May 2025, has been appointed CEO of Lululemon. O’Neill spent 27 years at Nike, where she spearheaded many of the firm’s growth and innovation initiatives. Prior to her president roles, O’Neill was VP and general manager of Nike’s global women’s division for seven years. O’Neill also serves on the boards of directors of consumer-facing companies including Spotify Technology and Hyatt Hotels. She will also join Lululemon’s board, and be based in Vancouver.

In a recent development, tech giant comments: “Heidi is an inspiring leader and proven, consumer-driven brand strategist, with a rare ability to both imagine a upcoming future for a brand and to create the structure and processes to deliver on that vision,” Marti Morfitt, executive chair of Lululemon’s board of directors, noted in a statement. “We selected Heidi because of the breadth of her experience, her demonstrated success delivering breakthrough ideas and initiatives at scale, and her ability to be a knowledgeable change and growth agent. We are excited to have Heidi join Lululemon and bring her strategic and creative vision to the company.”.

Background: Laura du Rusquec is stepping down from her role as CEO of Ganni to “pursue other opportunities”, according to the firm. She joined the Danish brand in April 2024, succeeding Andrea Baldo, and was previously deputy CEO at Balenciaga. Ganni has named Hans Hoegstedt as interim CEO, effective immediately; founders Nicolaj and Ditte Reffstrup will remain involved, the latter as creative director.

Organization comments: “The entire Ganni organization extends its sincere gratitude for Laura’s commitment and contribution over the last two years, and wishes her every success for the future,” the company noted in a statement.

It has been revealed that laura du Rusquec. Photo: Courtesy of Ganni.

Background: Apple has announced Tim Cook will step down as CEO in September, handing over to the company’s hardware engineering boss John Ternus and ending a 15-year tenure as Apple’s second-ever chief executive. Cook — who took over from Apple’s storied founder and CEO Steve Jobs in 2011, shortly before his death — will join the company’s board of directors as executive chair. In this role, Apple noted he will continue to assist the company by engaging with global policymakers, among other tasks.

During his tenure as CEO, Cook led Apple from a market cap of around $350 billion to $4 trillion — a more than 1,000% increase, according to the manufacturer. In the last 15 years, he’s overseen the introduction of several new products and services, including the Apple Watch, AirPods, the Apple Vision Pro, iCloud, Apple Pay, and the App Store.

Ternus has worked at Apple for 25 years, during which he has been instrumental in the introduction of several product lines, including the iPad, AirPods, and multiple generations of the iPhone.

Tech giant comments: “It has been the greatest privilege of my life to be the CEO of Apple and to have been trusted to lead such an extraordinary company,” Cook said in a statement. “John Ternus has the mind of an engineer, the soul of an innovator, and the heart to lead with integrity and honor.”.

Incoming CEO John Ternus (left) and outgoing CEO Tim Cook (right).

Background: Parisian brand Jacquemus has appointed Laetitia Manfredi as its chief product and merchandising officer. She has more than 20 years of experience across fashion and luxury, most recently serving as director of women’s accessories at Christian Dior Couture. At Jacquemus, Manfredi will be focusing on product growth to support the independent house’s global expansion plans, as well as leading the studio and merchandising into its next phase by leaning into the brand’s design codes. Manfredi will report to CEO Sarah Benady, while working closely with founding designer Simon Porte Jacquemus.

According to recent reports, background: Dolce & Gabbana Beauty has appointed Melinda Melrose, who rose to fame through Netflix’s Too Hot to Handle and Dated and Related, as its global makeup expert. She will be working with the Italian house on its makeup collections. The appointment marks a move away from employing traditional beauty experts to guide the makeup direction of luxury beauty brands; she has 1.4 million followers on Instagram.

Manufacturer comments: “With her iconic and instantly recognizable approach, Melinda brings to Dolce & Gabbana Beauty a bold, elevated aesthetic vision, skilfully blending technical expertise with a contemporary language that resonates with newly introduced generations seeking originality beyond the expected,” the brand noted in a statement.

According to recent reports, background: Sports brand Puma has appointed James Carnes as its first SVP of creative direction, reporting to chief brand officer Maria Valdes. In this newly created role, Carnes will align creative direction with the tech giant’s overall strategic ambitions through product innovation and excellence. With more than two decades of experience in the sports industry, including leadership positions at Adidas, he will help Puma in its turnaround to establish itself as a top three global sports brand.

Industry observers note that company comments: “James is a very highly regarded leader in our industry and he has been instrumental in shaping some of the most influential performance and lifestyle products, labels, and platforms. With a strong background and a deep understanding of both athletes and consumers, he will play an important role in getting consumers excited about Puma once again,“ Valdes stated in a statement.

Background: Andy Caine has been named chief innovation officer of Nike, reporting to chief innovation, design and product officer Phil McCartney. Caine has been with the company for more than 20 years, most recently as creative director of Nike Sportswear, where he translated performance innovation into lifestyle appeal and business growth. In his new role, Caine will guide Nike’s innovation initiatives across brands, sports, products, and platforms.

Sources indicate that background: Heather Archibald is joining Vuori as chief product officer. She joins from Rothy’s, where she was the shoe brand’s chief product and merchandising officer. Prior to this, she held roles at Title Nine, Restoration Hardware and Gap Inc. At Vuori, Archibald will lead the brand’s end-to-end product organization, overseeing design, development, merchandising, sourcing, and production strategy.

According to recent reports, manufacturer comments: “This is an exciting moment for Vuori as we continue to build on our strong momentum and invest in the capabilities that will carry us forward,” Vuori founder and CEO Joe Kudla remarked in a statement. “With Heather joining the brand, we’re reinforcing our commitment to a product-first approach — deepening innovation, sharpening storytelling and assortments, and bringing even greater rigor to how we scale while maintaining a deep connection with our consumers.”.

Background: Ralph Toledano has held some of the industry’s most prominent leadership roles, notably serving as CEO of Chloé from 1999 to 2010. He later joined Puig as president of its fashion division. From 2014 to 2022, he was president of the Fédération de la Haute Couture et de la Mode, where he now remains honorary president. In 2018, he became chair of Victoria Beckham, playing a key role in the brand’s growth alongside David Belhassen, founder of Neo Investment Partners, an investor in the label. In March 2026, Toledano stepped down from both his position as chair of Victoria Beckham Ltd and his role as senior partner at Neo Investment Partners.

In a recent development, comment: “It’s a natural evolution,” Toledano told Vogue Business. “There are many things I want to do: learn, write, and mentor fashion talents. Victoria Beckham is in good hands. The two CEOs, Sybille Darricarrère Lunel for fashion and Lauren Edelman for beauty, are excellent.”.

Background: Marta Lastra, who has served as Altuzarra president since January 2025, has been promoted to CEO of the New York brand. Since joining the fashion label, Lastra has played a pivotal role in strengthening the firm’s operational and strategic foundation. She will continue to oversee the company’s global strategy and next phase of growth, which includes expanding its physical footprint. Lastra succeeds founder and creative director Joseph Altuzarra, who took on the role following the departure of Shira Sue Carmi in late 2024.

According to recent reports, company comments: “Marta has been an exceptional leader and partner. Her deep understanding of the business, combined with her strategic mindset and operational expertise, has been invaluable to the company. As Altuzarra continues to grow, I am excited to focus more fully on the creative vision of the brand while working closely with Marta as she leads the company into its next chapter,” Altuzarra stated in a statement.

According to recent reports, background: Ulta Beauty has promoted Kristin Wolf to chief strategy and growth officer, to drive the retailer’s international expansion and long-term growth. Wolf has been with Ulta Beauty for almost seven years, having joined as VP of corporate strategy in 2019 and most recently serving as SVP of enterprise strategy and new growth. In her next role, Wolf will continue to oversee corporate strategy, development, and new growth initiatives.

Firm comments: “Kristin has been instrumental in establishing our Ulta Beauty Unleashed strategy and spearheading latest growth initiatives, including the launch of our wellness category and international expansion efforts,” CEO Kecia Steelman mentioned in a statement. “As we look to the future, we are confident that Kristin’s strategic leadership will be integral to achieving our vision of being the most-loved beauty destination.”.

It has been revealed that background: Matthew M. Williams is joining Oakley as creative director of its apparel, footwear, and accessories (AFA) business. The appointment comes after Travis Scott was named the brand’s chief visionary officer last June. Williams will lead Oakley AFA into its next chapter: under his direction, the offshoot will present both performance-driven and lifestyle collections, prioritizing product innovation across all categories, as Oakley repositions itself as a tech firm. The former Givenchy creative director is used to designing across brands and forms, having collaborated with the likes of Nike, Dior, Audemars Piguet, and more through his co-founded fashion label 1017 Alyx 9SM.

Company comments: “This is the ideal moment to welcome Matthew Williams to elevate Oakley’s AFA collections and expand the offering of one of the world’s most innovative brands. Sport performance, technology, and Oakley’s distinctive heritage will continue to shape the brand’s future collections with Matthew’s creative direction,” Francesco Milleri, chair and CEO of Oakley parent company EssilorLuxottica, mentioned in a statement.

Sources indicate that background: As it prepares for its next phase of global growth, On is updating its organizational structure. Co-founders David Allemann and Caspar Coppetti will serve as co-CEOs, while Martin Hoffmann step downs as CEO of the sportswear brand. Allemann and Coppetti will assume the position while remaining executive co-chairs, to facilitate their operational roles and execute the roadmap set out by themselves and Hoffman. The latter’s exit follows a 13-year tenure as CFO and five years as CEO, during which On evolved from a Swiss startup into a multi-billion-dollar business.

Meanwhile, chief innovation and operations officer Scott Maguire will be promoted to president and COO. He will be tasked with overseeing the entire value chain — from R&D and manufacturing, to marketing, global commercial operations, and technology.

It has been revealed that company comments: “From the early days through a landmark IPO, Martin’s commitment to our culture and financial discipline has been instrumental. It has been a privilege to work alongside him and we are deeply grateful for his partnership, his outstanding contribution, and the legacy he has built,” Caspar Coppetti said in a statement. Allemann added: “By unifying founder-led strategic intent with our operational core, we aim to move faster, stay relentlessly focused on product heat, and continue pushing the boundaries of what a sportswear brand can be.”.

Left to right: Scott Maguire, Olivier Bernhard, David Allemann, and Caspar Coppetti.

Industry observers note that background: Australian brand Zimmermann has appointed Roberto Eggs as CEO, who has been board director since March 2025. Eggs was most recently chief business and global market officer at Moncler, where he worked for over 10 years, before stepping down on March 1. Chris Olliver, who has been CEO of Zimmermann since 2005, will transition into the role of executive chair.

Company comments: “I’m delighted to welcome Roberto to Zimmermann, and look forward to working closely with him as we continue the brand’s strong global growth,” Olliver mentioned in a statement. “His leadership record speaks for itself, and his decision to join is a powerful endorsement of what our team has built and the opportunity ahead.”.

According to recent reports, background: Thomas Hézard, who has been promoted to chief product officer, joined Vestiaire Collective in 2019 after leading strategic initiatives for the luxury sector at BCG. He’s since held senior leadership roles at the former across operations, but most recently as chief strategy and people officer. Rémi Bouchez, now chief technology officer, joined Vestiare Collective in 2018, and has held several senior roles within the technology department, most recently as VP of engineering.

In their new positions, both will report to CEO Bernard Osta, who replaced former CEO Maximilian Bittner in October 2025. Together, Hézard and Bouchez will focus on the manufacturer’s product and technology strategy, “leveraging AI and placing innovation at the core of Vestiaire Collective’s mission”.

Firm comments: “I’m very excited about these strategic appointments. Thomas and Rémi will drive Vestiaire Collective’s innovation agenda, strengthening our leadership in the global fashion resale market, delivering enhanced user experience to our global community, and actively shaping the future of how people discover, engage with, and consume secondhand fashion,” Osta noted in a statement.

Sources indicate that background: Houlès started his career in telecom consulting, working for firms including Capgemini, before joining French media conglomerate Canal+ Group in 2012, becoming chief information officer by 2014. In 2016, he joined Renault Group as VP of sales and marketing information systems before being promoted to a dual role as deputy group chief information officer and Renault Digital managing director. At Kering, he will report to group chief operating officer Jean-Marc Duplaix (who is also now CEO of the Kering Jewelry division) and will join Kering’s executive committee.

Company comments: “Pierre Houlès’s expertise in large-scale transformation, the integration of complex systems, and the application of emerging technologies, notably artificial intelligence, will be instrumental in accelerating the development of a more integrated, innovative, and forward-looking group,” the company stated in a statement.

Industry observers note that background: Jean-Marc Duplaix, Kering’s chief operating officer, has also been appointed CEO of Kering Jewelry, a new entity designed to structure and accelerate the growth of the group’s jewelry business. The new entity brings together the group’s jewelry houses — Boucheron, Pomellato, Dodo, and Qeelin — as well as its industrial capabilities, including the Raselli Franco Group, which is currently being integrated. The CEOs of the group’s jewelry houses will report to Duplaix.

Industry observers note that organization comments: “With Kering Jewelry, we are giving the group a powerful and cohesive platform capable of supporting our houses’ ambitions in an area of expertise where creativity and excellence are inseparable,” Kering CEO Luca de Meo said in a statement. “I am delighted with the appointment of Jean-Marc: his experience will be instrumental in unlocking the group’s full potential in jewelry.”.

Background: Australian Wool Innovation (AWI), the woolgrowers association behind Woolmark, has appointed seasoned agriculture executive Bryan Fry as CEO, effective immediately. Fry most recently served as chairman and global CEO of Pernod Ricard Winemakers. He replaces John Roberts, who has led AWI since October 2021. Fry joins the organization at a critical juncture, as the Australian wool market implements its biggest price hike in three decades, and Woolmark continues its bid to get more designers to use merino wool — the primary motivation behind its annual talent competition, the International Woolmark Prize.

Manufacturer comments: “Bryan’s career is distinguished by a rare combination of hands-on agricultural experience as an agronomist alongside deep expertise in international marketing, brand development and commercial strategy,” AWI chairman George Millington said in a statement. “This unique blend of skills positions him strongly to lead the research, development and marketing organization for Australian woolgrowers, including AWI’s global Woolmark program.”.

Recent findings suggest that background: Tag Heuer Americas president Béatrice Goasglas has been promoted to CEO of the LVMH-owned watchmaker. Goasglas began her career in 2007 at Sephora as a CRM project manager consultant, before various roles at L’Oréal, The Kooples, and French ready-to-wear group SMCP. Goasglas’s career at Tag Heuer began in 2018 as VP of digital and client experience, before taking on the role of Asia-Pacific managing director and most recently Americas president. The appointment follows former CEO Antoine Pin’s exit from the brand in mid-January.

According to recent reports, company comments: “Béatrice has had an outstanding career at Tag Heuer, and I am delighted that she will be taking the helm of this iconic watchmaking maison,” Stéphane Bianchi, LVMH Group managing director and CEO of LVMH Watches & Jewelry remarked in a statement. “Her deep knowledge of the brand, combined with her leadership and unparalleled commitment, will enable Tag Heuer to reach upcoming heights, and to continue embodying the very highest watchmaking quality and avant-garde spirit so dear to the maison.”.

It has been revealed that background: Jimmy Choo has appointed Andy Holmes as its next chief financial officer, replacing Richard Kozlowski, who will retire at the end of March. Holmes, who was most recently CFO and COO of British menswear brand Dunhill, brings more than two decades of senior leadership experience from various luxury brands. At Jimmy Choo, he will help shape the strategic direction of the London-based accessories house as it enters a latest phase of growth.

According to recent reports, tech giant comments: “We are delighted to welcome Andy to the leadership team. His extensive financial expertise, commercial acumen, and deep understanding of the luxury market will be invaluable as we continue to deliver on our growth strategy,” CEO Hannah Colman said in a statement.

Background: Philippe Farnier has been named deputy CEO of Parfums Christian Dior. He will report to Véronique Courtois, chairman and CEO of Parfums Christian Dior and the LVMH Beauty Division. In his fresh role, Farnier will collaborate closely with Courtois on key strategic initiatives and oversee the commercial and omnichannel activities across the division. Farnier has held senior roles at Yves Saint Laurent Beauté and Rémy Cointreau, and he previously worked at Parfums Christian Dior as France general manager in 2008.

Recent findings suggest that company comments: “I am absolutely delighted of Philippe’s appointment as deputy CEO of Parfums Christian Dior and LVMH Beauty Division. Philippe’s exceptional leadership, international strategic acumen, and deep industry knowledge make him the perfect partner to take over this strategic role,” Véronique Courtois, chairman and CEO of Parfums Christian Dior, said in a statement.

In a recent development, background: Laura Stauth has been appointed SVP of sales for Salomon, a role she joins from VF Corp-owned Vans, where she most recently held the same role. At Salomon, Stauth will lead the brand’s North American softgoods sales, with a focus on wholesale expansion. She joins recent additions to the team: Aaron Sullivan, VP of digital experience and e-commerce, and LeeAnn Fallon, vice president of retail for Salomon North America, who joined the brand in July and September of 2025, respectively.

Industry observers note that company comments: “Laura, Aaron and LeeAnn bring a powerful combination of strategic vision, operational excellence, and deep wholesale, retail, e-commerce and digital expertise,” Steve Doolan, Salomon’s GM and president of the Americas, said in a statement. “As we continue to build momentum, their leadership will be instrumental in expanding our market presence, elevating our retail partnerships, and driving sustainable growth across all channels and product categories.”.

In a recent development, background: Chloé COO Yves Cauchon has been appointed CEO of LVMH Métiers d’Art, the luxury group’s dedicated craft arm. LVMH introduced the division in 2015 to preserve and access the artisanal skills and raw materials of 17 businesses spanning five pillars: sustainable farming, leather and exotic leather tanning, detailed metalwork production, precious fibers and textiles manufacturing, and innovation. Cauchon will be tasked with overseeing the supply chains and strategic savoir-faire of these businesses, while upholding LVMH’s environmental protection and social responsibility.

Sources indicate that firm comments: “Yves has an essential role in orchestrating the development and transformation of LVMH Métiers d’Art, in close collaboration with the industrial entities of Métiers d’Art and the group’s maisons. He will be responsible for ensuring the sustainability of savoir-faire and the operational excellence of all métiers with a view to creating sustainable value and innovation,” Ludovic Pauchard, industrial and craftsmanship director at LVMH Group, said in a statement.

It has been revealed that background: Abraham Ortuño, founder of ready-to-wear brand Abra, has been appointed to creatively lead product and brand communication for footwear brand Camper, as well as its avant-garde diffusion line, Camperlab. The hire marks a fresh chapter for the Spanish organization, as it hopes to reinforce its cultural relevance, commitment to design innovation, and Mediterranean identity. Before founding Abra in 2019, Ortuño made a name for himself designing footwear in collaboration with various fashion houses, from Loewe’s broken eggs sandals to Jacquemus’s double-stacked kitten heels. The designer will make his debut for the brand during the Fall/Winter 2027 season.

Manufacturer comments: “Abraham represents a latest generation of creative leadership. His deep understanding of footwear, combined with a strong cultural sensibility and international perspective, makes him the ideal person to guide Camper into its next phase. We believe his vision will strengthen our design identity while opening new creative territories,” Camper CEO Miguel Fluxà noted in a statement.

Sources indicate that background: Amy Raimondi started her career in the Saks Fifth Avenue merchandising team nearly 20 years ago, working her way up to VP of brand partnerships and buying for women’s contemporary ready-to-wear at Saks Fifth Avenue and Neiman Marcus. Now, as SVP of women’s apparel buying, Raimondi will oversee contemporary, evening, lifestyle, lingerie, outerwear, swim, and children’s collections for Saks Fifth Avenue and Neiman Marcus, reporting to chief buying officer Paolo Riva.

Background: Stéphane Noël, who has 30 years of experience leading large-scale manufacturing operations, has joined Kering as chief industrial officer. Much like group CEO Luca de Meo, Noël comes from the automotive industry, having served most recently at ​car parts manufacturer Forvia. At the luxury group, he will be tasked with restructuring its industry division, which de Meo unveiled as part of Kering’s new organizational structure. The focus will be on strengthening production efficiency for all Kering houses, by integrating purchasing, manufacturing, supply chain, quality, as well as research and development. Noël will report directly to de Meo.

Organization comments: “I am delighted to welcome leaders who are recognized in their complementary areas of expertise to accelerate the transformation we have initiated. We are clarifying the organization, connecting the teams and ensuring efficiency across the group to give our houses the means to go faster and further,” de Meo stated in a statement.

Background: Cimarron Nix has been promoted from Nike’s VP of global apparel and accessories manufacturing to chief sustainability officer, leading the sportswear giant’s global sustainability team. She joined Nike in 2017, but has spent more than a decade leading policy and program development in responsible sourcing and sustainability.

According to recent reports, background: Anish Melwani, who has been chair and CEO of LVMH North America since 2016, is departing the group. During his tenure, Melwani successfully grew LVMH’s North American presence, alongside launching several global initiatives. He will be departing in April, following a transition period with Alexandra Winokur, formerly Christian Dior Couture Americas president since 2023. Winokur has been promoted to deputy CEO of LVMH North America, and will report to Americas chair Michael Burke. Before LVMH, she worked at Marc Jacobs, Tiffany & Co., and Cartier, the latter of which as SVP of commercial.

In a recent development, organization comment: “North America is of paramount strategic importance to LVMH and the enduring desirability of our maisons. I am pleased to welcome Alexandra, who will undoubtedly help us further grow our presence and uphold our uncompromising standards of excellence throughout our operations,” Burke noted. “My deepest thanks go to Anish for his passionate leadership and impactful contribution to our group and maisons in North America. He leaves behind an extremely committed team, whose outstanding management of the local business is widely recognized by the industry.”.

According to recent reports, background: Tyler Reddien has been named chief financial officer and chief operating officer of Capri Holdings, reflecting the organization’s “ongoing commitment to strengthening its leadership team… and positioning the company for future growth across its portfolio of luxury brands”. Tyler most recently served as CFO of The Body Shop and previously held senior leadership positions at cosmetics and personal care company Natura & Co Holding.

Industry observers note that firm comments: “Tyler is an exceptional finance and operations leader whose strategic mindset and international experience make him ideally suited to help position Capri’s future growth and long-term value creation,” noted John D. Idol, chairman and CEO of Capri Holdings.

In a recent development, background: Jenny Kim, who most recently led Americas marketing at Bottega Veneta, has been appointed chief communications and image officer of Dior Americas. Prior to Bottega, Kim held various senior leadership roles at Proenza Schouler, Prada, PR Consulting, and Helmut Lang. At Dior, she will report globally to Olivier Bialobos, deputy managing director of global communications and image for Christian Dior Couture and Parfums Christian Dior. Locally, Kim will report to Christian Dior Couture Americas president Charlotte Holman Ros, as well as Olivier Teboul, president of Parfums Christian Dior North America.

Firm comments: “Jenny’s experience and expertise will help deliver even more exceptional experiences to our clients and affirm a positioning fully aligned with the expression of the house’s new artistic direction,” Bialobos remarked in a statement.

Industry observers note that background: Liran Peterzil has been named as chief marketing officer of Valentino, succeeding Yigit Turhan, who is exiting after five years in various roles at the firm. Peterzil, who will oversee the development of Valentino’s global brand strategy, will report to Riccardo Bellini. Peterzil previously held senior roles at Giorgio Armani and CAA.

In a recent development, background: Calvin McDonald, a three-time CEO, most recently of Lululemon, is joining beauty company Wella as chief executive offer to oversee portfolio brands including Wella, Briogeo, Opi, Clairol, and GHD. McDonald will be primarily focusing on scaling the company’s categories, product assortment, and investments.

It has been revealed that organization comment: “As a three-time CEO, Calvin brings decades of experience at industry-leading global consumer brands and retail businesses. His proven ability to drive results through product differentiation, category expansion, and smart investments will help us win in the dynamic beauty sector,” remarked Glenn Murphy, Wella’s executive chair, in a statement.

Sources indicate that calvin McDonald. Photo: Courtesy of Wella.

Background: Target has announced newly introduced executive leadership changes to accelerate its growth. Cara Sylvester has been named chief merchandising officer, while Lisa Roath has been named chief operating officer, the manufacturer shared in a press release. It also said Michelle Mesenburg will become senior vice president and chief brand officer. All three executives have long tenures at the company.

According to recent reports, organization comments: “Cara and Lisa are proven leaders who deeply know our business and can drive change that delivers results,” CEO Michael Fiddelke noted in a statement. “As they lead two of our most critical functions, we’ve got the right foundation to make bold, strategic moves and execute our plans for Target’s future.”.

In a recent development, background: Ying McGuire has been named as CEO of global non-profit alliance Cascale (formerly the Sustainable Apparel Coalition) at a pivotal moment for the organization. Cascale owns and operates the Higg Index, a sustainability data platform used by more than 40,000 fashion and textile organizations globally, and is in the midst of scaling its collective action programs. McGuire brings deep expertise in multi-stakeholder initiatives and non-profit transformation, having recently served as CEO and president of the US Minority Supplier Development Council. She replaces interim CEO Harsh Saini, who will continue to advise Cascale until the end of June.

According to recent reports, background: Thierry Conrad Reutenauer has been promoted to chief marketing officer of Loewe. Reutenauer hailed from Bottega Veneta to join the Spanish house as global communications director in October 2025. Before joining the Kering group, he led public relations and events at Richemont-owned Chloé, and worked at London-based agency Karla Otto. As CMO, Reutenauer will oversee all marketing teams and touchpoints for the brand, from art direction and events, to editorial and social media.

In a recent development, background: Cheryl Han has been named chief marketing and digital officer of Saks Global, a newly created role in which she will oversee the firm’s marketing and e-commerce. Previously, she was chief digital officer at Saks Global, a post she left in August 2025. Before Saks Global, she briefly held the same role at Neiman Marcus (until Saks’s acquisition of Neiman was completed). Prior to this, Han rose up the ranks at Bergdorf Goodman.

Firm comments: “We are pleased to announce the appointment of Cheryl Han as chief marketing and digital officer of Saks Global as we continue to take decisive steps to position the company for sustainable, profitable growth,” a Saks Global spokesperson mentioned in a statement. “This newly created position brings two key pillars together under one leader and reflects the critical role that marketing and digital play in driving sales and customer engagement across all channels. In this role, Han will oversee Saks Global’s end-to-end marketing strategy and execution, and will also be responsible for the e-commerce businesses for all banners.”.

Sources indicate that background: Emilie Leblanc will assume the fresh role of global marketing and communications director at Bottega Veneta. She was most recently global communications director at Celine in Paris, but spent most of her career at Saint Laurent. At Bottega, Leblanc will report to chief merchandising and marketing officer Samuel Diep, while inheriting the responsibilities of Thierry Conrad Reutenauer, who moved to Loewe as global communications director in 2025.
